question: If {x²} - sqrt {13} x + 1 = 0, then (x³ + x⁻³) is equal to:
solution:
Given:

{x²} - √ {13} x + 1 = 0

Concept used:

if a + 1/a = b

Then,

a3 + 1/a3 = (b)3 - 3b

Calculation:

{x²} - √ {13} x + 1 = 0

⇒ {x²} + 1 = √ {13} x

⇒ x + 1/x = √13 [By dividing x from both sides]

Now,

(x3 + x-3) = (x³ + 1/x³)

⇒ (x3 + x-3) = (√13)³ - 3 × √13

⇒ (x3 + x-3) = 13√13 - 3√13

⇒ (x3 + x-3) = 10√13

∴ Required answer is **10√13.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

(a + 1/a) = b

On cubing both sides we'll get,

(a + 1/a)3 = b3 

⇒ a3 + (1/a)3 + 3(a)(1/a)(a + 1/a) = b3 

⇒ a3 + (1/a)3 + 3(a + 1/a) = b3 

⇒ a3 + (1/a)3 + 3(b) = b3 

⇒ a3 + (1/a)3 = b3 - 3(b)
